executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate repeated PAHO alerts (November 2025 and March 2026), signaling persistent zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas region and warranting Critical-level attention as a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential. Mpox, dengue, measles, and chikungunya are simultaneously circulating across the Americas, compounding healthcare system burden alongside a seasonal influenza transition in both hemispheres. Pertussis resurgence has prompted two separate PAHO alerts within three months, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome adds further pressure as a high-fatality BSL-3 pathogen requiring close monitoring.
bottomLine: A convergence of A(H5N1) zoonotic risk, mpox spread, dengue surge, pertussis resurgence, and hantavirus detections across the Americas represents a multi-pathogen threat environment demanding coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued within four months (November 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained activity
Repeated zoonotic spillover events in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human transmission risk
BSL-3 select agent with documented pandemic potential and high case fatality rate
threats.action: Activate enhanced One Health surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce biosafety protocols at affected farms; accelerate prepandemic vaccine stockpiling and antiviral deployment planning

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating increased case detection
BSL-3 pathogen with case fatality rates exceeding 35% in some regions
Seasonal rodent population dynamics may amplify exposure risk heading into 2026
threats.action: Strengthen rodent control programs and public education in endemic areas; ensure diagnostic capacity and ICU preparedness in affected health systems; enforce BSL-3 specimen handling protocols

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained community-level spread following the 2022-2024 global outbreak trajectory
Risk of clade Ib importation from Africa adds potential severity escalation
threats.action: Expand JYNNEOS vaccination programs targeting high-risk populations; reinforce case detection and contact tracing; coordinate with ECDC on importation risk to Europe

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Americas region experienced record dengue burden in 2024-2025 with continued hyperendemicity
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases severe dengue risk
threats.action: Scale vector control interventions ahead of peak transmission season; ensure blood supply safety; deploy dengue rapid diagnostics to under-resourced health facilities

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates within three months (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating accelerating resurgence
Waning vaccine immunity and vaccine hesitancy driving renewed circulation
Infant mortality risk from incomplete vaccination schedules
threats.action: Intensify Tdap booster campaigns for adolescents, adults, and pregnant women; audit vaccination coverage rates nationally; investigate macrolide resistance patterns in circulating strains

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Virus Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation straining healthcare systems
PAHO April 2026 alert marks start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Five consecutive ECDC weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) maintaining active monitoring
threats.action: Monitor influenza strain match with 2026 Southern Hemisphere vaccine formulation; reinforce hospital surge capacity planning; prioritize RSV monoclonal antibody prophylaxis for high-risk infants

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or spillover risk
Epizootics in non-human primates are early warning indicators of human transmission risk
Gaps in vaccination coverage in endemic zones create outbreak vulnerability
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations in endemic areas; strengthen epizootic surveillance in primate populations; ensure adequate yellow fever vaccine supply at entry points

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert February 2026 indicating active cases in the region
Post-pandemic immunization gaps have reduced herd immunity below the 95% threshold in multiple countries
Risk of resurgence in urban centers with low vaccination coverage
threats.action: Conduct supplementary immunization activities targeting under-vaccinated communities; investigate outbreak clusters for importation sources; reinforce routine childhood vaccination schedules

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were detected in surveillance reporting during this period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a Tier 1 select agent with pandemic potential, triggered two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), reflecting persistent zoonotic activity in the Americas requiring Critical-level response. Hantavirus (Sin Nombre/Andes), a BSL-3 pathogen with high mortality, was the subject of a PAHO alert in December 2025, indicating ongoing case detection in the Americas region. Both pathogens require strict BSL-3 specimen handling and enhanced One Health surveillance coordination.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence despite vaccination suggests potential surveillance gap but macrolide resistance in Bordetella pertussis warrants investigation given two alerts in three months
Influenza antiviral resistance monitoring required as H5N1 activity persists across the Americas, particularly oseltamivir resistance profiling in avian strains
emergingPatterns: Dual-wave pertussis alert pattern (December 2025 and March 2026) suggests accelerating resurgence potentially linked to post-pandemic immunization deficits and waning booster immunity
Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden (influenza A/B, RSV, pertussis) risks healthcare system saturation during the Southern Hemisphere winter 2026 season
Repeated H5N1 alerts across two calendar years indicate endemic-level zoonotic pressure in the Americas rather than isolated spillover events
Co-circulation of multiple arboviral threats (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in overlapping geographic zones creates diagnostic confusion and compounded vector control demands
Post-pandemic immunity debt continues to manifest across vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis, signaling structural vaccination system weaknesses
